items.t: Patakha stock picks! ICICI Bank, BEL, 6 other stocks with 62% to buy this Samvat 2023. See full list
sum: As investors enter Samvat 2083, the landscape calls for selectivity rather than indiscriminate optimism. Global uncertainties, fluctuating capital flows and evolving market expectations continue to influence equity performance. In this environment, sustainable wealth creation is likely to depend less on broad-based market movements and more on identifying businesses capable of delivering consistent earnings growth. Here are 8 stocks PL Capital is bullish on.

PL Capital has set a target price of Rs 490 for Bharat Electronics (BEL), implying an upside of 24% from current levels. The company has a strong order book of Rs 68,720 crore, equivalent to 2.3x its trailing 12-month sales, providing healthy execution visibility. Key programmes, including Electronic Fuses, LCA MK1A, LR-SAM, BMP-2 upgrades, Ashwini Radar and EW Suites for Mi-17, account for around Rs 17,600 crore. The Rs 20,000 crore NGC opportunity is expected to translate into staggered orders from GSL and GRSE, largely by the end of FY27. Orders worth Rs 30,000 crore for QRSAM are also expected shortly, with BEL well positioned to retain its role given its decade-long development experience.

PL Capital has set a target price of Rs 6,579 for Britannia Industries, implying an upside of 37.5% from current levels. The brokerage maintains a high-conviction view on the company, supported by its leadership in the biscuits and bakery segments, sustained growth in signature brands and improving scalability and profitability across adjacencies. Its signature brands grew 3x faster than the rest of the portfolio in FY26. A robust innovation pipeline focused on region- and channel-specific offerings, alongside premiumisation, further supports the growth outlook. The complete resolution of the dual-pricing issue is also expected to restore volume stability and support a recovery in growth.

PL Capital has set a target price of Rs 1,900 for ICICI Bank, implying an upside of 21% from current levels. The brokerage considers ICICI Bank the best-performing bank in terms of earnings quality, supported by a strong balance sheet. Its CET-1 ratio stands at 16%, while the loan-to-deposit ratio is maintained between 86% and 89%, and the liquidity coverage ratio remains adequate at 126%.

US Midterm Election results lift banking, financial stocks - SBI Cards, Bajaj Finance, Axis, ICICI Bank surge up to 6%
sum: Banking and financial stocks rallied sharply on Thursday, November 5, outperforming the broader market as investors cheered Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, renewed foreign investor buying and a steep decline in crude oil prices.

The election outcome raised hopes of reduced geopolitical tensions and potentially lower trade uncertainty, while Brent crude's slide to a two-month low provided additional relief to the oil-import-dependent Indian economy.

The Nifty Financial Services index surged nearly 3% intraday, while the Nifty Bank index advanced 2.2%, outperforming the Nifty 50, which gained nearly 2%. The rally reflected improving investor appetite for financial stocks amid a broader recovery in domestic equities.
Buying was broad-based across banking and financial stocks, with all constituents of the Nifty Bank index trading in positive territory.

Among financial stocks, SBI Cards led the gains, rising over 6%. Shriram Finance, Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company, Bajaj Finance and HDFC AMC also advanced over 5% each. Muthoot Finance gained 4.5%, while Bajaj Finserv, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, REC and LIC Housing Finance rose over 2% each.
Within the banking pack, AU Small Finance Bank led the Nifty Bank gainers, climbing over 4%. IndusInd Bank, Axis Bank, IDFC First Bank and ICICI Bank advanced between 3% and 4% each.
Canara Bank and HDFC Bank gained over 2% each, while Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank, State Bank of India and Kotak Mahindra Bank added over 1% each.

sum: Stock market recap: Indian equities extended their rally for a fourth straight session on Tuesday, as a steep fall in crude oil prices, sustained foreign buying, and growing hopes of capital gains tax relief kept bulls firmly in control.

Nifty 50 rose 370.05 points, or 1.58%, to close at its day's high of 23,810.85, while Sensex jumped 1,225.07 points, or 1.62%, to settle at 76,917.85. Brent crude slipped to around $105 a barrel, about 11% below Friday's six-month high of $118, on optimism over diplomatic efforts to end the Iran conflict.

Foreign investors bought about ₹3,115 crore of Indian shares on Monday, adding to the momentum. Financials, FMCG, and Realty led the gains, while capital market stocks such as BSE jumped up to 8% on hopes of tax relief. Bharti Airtel rose about 5%, Asian Paints nearly 4%, and HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and IndiGo about 3% each. IT, Metal, and Pharma stocks lagged, with ONGC, Power Grid, NTPC, and Sun Pharma among the losers, while Reliance saw mild profit-taking. Breadth was positive, with 2,127 stocks advancing, 1,477 stocks declining, and 109 remaining unchanged. The U.S. midterm election results, due after Indian market hours, will be closely watched.

- Why it’s recommended: Strong growth in high-margin specialty films (Paint Protection Films, Sun Control Films and Architectural Films) supported by capacity expansion and backward integration into TPU manufacturing. The global export-led business has a presence in 90+ countries and vertically integrated manufacturing, providing pricing power, cost efficiencies, and market-share gains in specialty films.
- Key metrics: P/E: 37.97, 52-week high: ₹7,990.00, volume: ₹73.51 crore

- Risk factors: Exposure to volatility in crude-linked raw material prices and foreign exchange fluctuations due to significant export dependence. Regulatory risks in the sun-control film segment and demand sensitivity to automotive and construction industry cycles.

- Why it’s recommended: Strong positioning in chronic and sub-chronic therapies (women's healthcare, cardio-diabetes, pain management and urology), which contribute over 70% of revenue and continue to outperform the Indian Pharma Market.

Muhurat Trading Picks: Adani Ports, Info Edge to Kotak Bank - ICICI Sec recommends these 10 stocks to buy on Diwali
sum: Despite the recent correction in Indian equities, ICICI Securities remains constructive on the market, arguing that the selloff reflects external pressures rather than any meaningful deterioration in corporate earnings. With Q2 FY27 earnings showing strong growth, valuations slipping below their long-term averages, and the domestic earnings cycle gaining momentum, the brokerage believes the risk-reward equation is turning more favourable for investors.

It expects the Nifty 50 to deliver healthy double-digit returns over the next 12 months, with quality mid- and small-cap stocks offering opportunities as markets increasingly shift their focus from liquidity and valuations to earnings delivery.

The brokerage's Muhurat Trading picks include Venus Pipes and Tubes, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Zydus Lifesciences, Info Edge, Adani Ports and SEZ, Apollo Micro Systems, Neogen Chemicals, Indian Hotels, Saregama India and Ethos.

ICICI Securities expects Kotak Mahindra Bank to deliver 20–22% advances growth, supported by a gradual recovery in net interest margins and sustained moderation in credit costs. These factors are likely to drive earnings growth and improve return on assets (RoA) over FY27–FY28, the brokerage said.
The brokerage values the standalone bank at 2.4 times its FY28 book value and its subsidiaries at ₹127 per share. It has maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a target price of ₹540.
Key risks: ICICI Securities flagged two key risks: an adverse change in the business mix that could dilute margins, and slower-than-expected business growth.

ICICI Securities noted that Venus Pipes and Tubes has recently completed a fresh equity raise through a preferential allotment, with the proceeds primarily intended to pare debt. This is expected to significantly strengthen the company's balance sheet and could make it net debt-free in FY27E. The resulting reduction in interest expenses is likely to support profitability and prove accretive to earnings per share (EPS), the brokerage said.

Massive surge! Reliance Industries shares up 12% after Q2; add ₹2 lakh cr in mcap — when did RIL last rally this much?
sum: The shares finished Monday’s trade with a solid 12% jump to settle at ₹1,300 on NSE, their highest level since early September. The stock last posted a comparable single-day surge in April 2020. Given its heavyweight status in the Nifty 50, the rally also lifted the index by 1.7%, even as tensions in West Asia remained elevated.

For long-term Reliance Industries shareholders, the sharp rise has revived confidence in the stock, which had been trending lower since the start of 2026. The shares closed in the red in eight of the previous 10 months. Despite Monday’s rebound, the stock remains down 17.22% so far this year.

The double-digit jump in the stock added ₹1.84 lakh crore to the company’s market capitalisation, taking it to ₹17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India’s most valuable listed company.

At its peak of ₹1,611, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the ₹21 lakh crore mark in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve this milestone.

Meanwhile, investors in the Reliance Group have another reason to celebrate, as its telecom arm, Jio Platforms, made a blockbuster stock market debut last week, listing at ₹1,440 apiece, a premium of 21.3% over its issue price.

Reliance Industries Ltd reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹29,550 crore for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), marking a 33.8% increase from ₹22,092 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record ₹62,409 crore.

The strong performance was primarily driven by a recovery in the oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, where EBITDA surged 67.9% to ₹25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to ₹2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

Jio Platforms vs Bharti Airtel shares: Which telecom stock to buy after Reliance arm’s IPO listing? Experts suggestions
sum: The listing of Jio Platforms has put the spotlight on India’s telecom sector, with investors now weighing whether the newly listed Reliance Industries-backed company or established rival Bharti Airtel offers a better investment opportunity.

Jio Platforms shares have surged nearly 28% from their issue price of ₹1,119 since making their market debut on Wednesday, 28 October, taking its market capitalisation to nearly ₹13.18 lakh crore and making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries. The strong debut and subsequent gains follow an IPO that attracted bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, has built a strong long-term track record, with its shares delivering returns of 586.10% over the past decade and 187.07% over five years. However, the stock remains down 6.64% so far in 2026. With Jio commanding a substantial valuation and Airtel offering an established earnings track record, which telecom stock should investors consider now? Experts weigh in on their growth prospects, valuations and investment appeal.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, remains a stronger proposition for investors seeking earnings visibility, higher ARPU, robust cash flows and disciplined capital allocation. Experts say investors should weigh valuations, earnings growth and execution risks before choosing between the two telecom stocks.

Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said Jio’s listing at a valuation of around ₹10.3 lakh crore places it among India’s top five companies by market capitalisation from day one. This, he said, changes the investment question from assessing the company’s growth potential to evaluating the returns investors can realistically expect from current levels. Companies of this scale rarely grow significantly faster than the broader economy, making low double-digit annual returns a reasonable base case.

He also noted that ARPU growth in India has historically been uneven, with increases largely coming through tariff hikes in 2019, 2021 and 2024. These hikes have typically required coordinated moves by all three telecom operators and have depended on regulatory considerations, making it difficult to factor in consistent ARPU growth over a 10-year investment horizon.

items.t: Kotak Mahindra Bank stock reaches record high as outlook brightens
sum: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares reached a record high on Thursday, October 29, as improving growth prospects and expectations for stronger earnings lifted investor sentiment. The Economic Times reported that the shares closed at INR 457 on the BSE, up 3.86 percent from the previous close, after touching INR 460 intraday.

The report said analysts expect earnings to improve as credit growth accelerates, funds raised through foreign-currency non-resident deposits are deployed and higher lending rates pass through. Better asset quality, lower credit costs and improved cost ratios are also expected to support profitability.

Axis Securities expects Kotak Mahindra Bank to deliver a return on assets of 2.1 to 2.2 percent and a return on equity of 12 to 14 percent over fiscal 2027 to fiscal 2029. The brokerage said those measures would place the bank second among large private-sector lenders, behind ICICI Bank.

Kotak Mahindra Bank's investor-relations page reports consolidated second-quarter profit after tax of INR 5,645 crore and customer assets of INR 699,250 crore. Standalone deposits reached INR 651,491 crore, while the net interest margin stood at 4.31 percent.

The bank also reported a 22.4 percent capital adequacy ratio, a 22.1 percent common-equity tier-one ratio and annualised returns on assets and equity of 2.10 percent and 11.70 percent, respectively. These figures give investors a reference point for assessing whether the expected recovery in growth can translate into more durable profitability.

Kotak Mahindra Bank is an Indian financial-services group with banking, lending, deposits and related customer-asset businesses. Its operations serve retail, corporate and other banking customers through a nationwide branch network and digital platforms. The available company material identifies the bank as a diversified Indian private-sector lender, but does not establish a directly comparable competitor set for this report.
Indian equities remain the broader market context for Kotak Mahindra Bank, with current market reports covering the regional investment backdrop.

IDBI Bank shares fall 7% as investors book profit after Fairfax deal gets cabinet nod
sum: The stock had climbed to Rs 93.60 on Wednesday, its highest level in nearly two weeks, taking IDBI Bank’s market capitalisation above Rs 1 lakh crore. The rally followed the Cabinet’s approval of the sale of the government’s and LIC’s combined stake to Fairfax Financial Holdings’ subsidiary, M/s 10955230 Canada Inc., for Rs 52,878.08 crore.
Also Read |Redington could gain as memory shortage reshapes ICT distribution; brokerage sees 20% upside

The deal marks a major step in the lender’s transformation after years of financial stress. Fairfax’s bid of Rs 81 per share was above the Rs 75.99 average fair valuation arrived at by two independent professional valuation agencies.

The government will retain a 15% stake in IDBI Bank, while LIC will hold 19% after the transaction. The successful bidder will also have to go through the RBI’s ‘fit & proper’ assessment and secure other regulatory approvals before the deal is completed.
Also Read |Jio IPO fever grips telecom stocks: Airtel, Vodafone Idea & others rise up to 4%

IDBI Bank today looks very different from the lender that once needed repeated government support. Its gross NPA ratio has fallen from 31.78% in September 2018 to 2.32% in March 2026, while net NPAs have dropped from 17.30% to 0.15%.

The improvement has also shown up in profitability and growth. IDBI Bank reported a net profit of Rs 9,513 crore in FY26, while its total business rose 18% year-on-year to Rs 6.27 lakh crore as of September 30. Its latest quarterly business update showed deposits rising 17% to Rs 3.56 lakh crore and net advances growing 18% to Rs 2.72 lakh crore.

Bank of Baroda shares drop 3% after NMC Healthcare founder BR Shetty files $15 bn lawsuit; lender issues c
sum: Bank of Baroda shares tumbled to Rs 230.40 apiece on NSE. This came after BR Shetty’s reported lawsuit, filed at the Bombay High Court, sought $5 billion in direct damages for alleged fraud and negligence, $5 billion in consequential damages and $5 billion in compensation for reputational harm arising from various actions taken by the bank, including a lookout circular issued against him. He also sought 18% interest on the first $10 billion, the ET report added.
Also read | Bank of Baroda to pay $600 million to settle NMC Health insolvency claims

Shetty’s lawsuit names Bank of Baroda, many of its current and former executives, former NMC employees, along with other individuals and companies, ET reported. His case is linked to one in the UAE that Bank of Baroda settled in July by paying roughly $600 million (around Rs 5,700 crore) to the administrators of the insolvent NMC and its affiliates. Administrators of the UAE-based healthcare group had accused Bank of Baroda of facilitating improper transactions in cahoots with Shetty, without doing due diligence and following proper anti-money-laundering and customer verification processes.

UAE-based healthcare provider NMC Health was declared insolvent in 2020 after it was found that it had hidden more than $4 billion in debt. Besides BoB, other creditors to the company are Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, Dubai Islamic Bank, Emirates NBD among others.
Following the sharp drop in share price, Bank of Baroda issued a clarification to exchanges, stating that it has not been served with such a suit.

Bank of Baroda shares have fallen more than 1% in a week and nearly 3% in a month, with the stock overall being down 23% in 2026 so far, underperforming the Nifty Next 50 index which is down only 1% during the same time.

The shares of the PSU lender have dropped over 12% in one year. In the longer term, the stock delivered positive returns of nearly 14% in three years and 161% in five years. The company’s market capitalisation stands at around Rs 1.2 lakh crore.
